# My Man

> My Man is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Mac app, with a Linux companion for agents, that gives people and their AI agents local screenshots, annotation, screen recording, meeting transcripts, dictation, notes, and searchable memory. Everything runs on-device and is saved as plain Markdown in `~/MyManBrain`. Agents such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Grok Bot use it through two local MCP servers (`myman-brain`, read-only search with citations; `myman-app`, over 120 permission-controlled app actions) or through the `myman` JSON CLI. All agent permissions start off and only the user can turn them on in Settings → Agents.

Key facts:
- Install: download the Mac app from https://muckstack.com/download/myman, open it once, and install Node.js 22+. Both MCP servers are then at `~/MyManBrain/tools/server.mjs` and `~/MyManBrain/tools/app-server.mjs`.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add myman-brain -- node ~/MyManBrain/tools/server.mjs` and `claude mcp add myman-app -- node ~/MyManBrain/tools/app-server.mjs`.
- CLI: `/Applications/My Man.app/Contents/Resources/myman` (`myman doctor --json`, `myman actions`, `myman screenshot --mode agent --json`). Results are JSON; long work returns a job ID.
- Check permissions before acting with `myman doctor --json` or the `myman_app_capabilities` MCP tool. Agents cannot grant themselves permissions.
- No cloud relay, account, or API key. Requires macOS 14.2+ (screen recording needs macOS 15+).

## Saved people resolution (candidate)

- CLI: `myman people resolve --names '["jilles","harshil"]' --limit 5 --json`. Action `people.resolve`; MCP `myman_app_people_resolve`. Requires a new human-enabled, default-off `people_read` grant and named-agent scope. `doctor` reports the grant; agents cannot enable it.
- Mac uses saved People.swift records and visible meeting participants. Linux/Omarchy uses the existing `people.md` export only; missing export returns `unsupported_on_platform` after grant checks. Hidden people are not recovered from old meeting exports. No Contacts, live calendar, accounts or network lookup.
- Results preserve input order and return `resolved`, `ambiguous`, `missing_email`, `needs_confirmation` or `not_found`, plus candidates, total and truncated. Ambiguity is computed before limiting candidates. Never choose an ambiguous/prefix candidate automatically or invent an email. Resolution never books or invites.
- Limits: 1–20 names, 200 characters per name, 1–10 candidates each. Root/Linux candidate 0.14.0, Brain companion 0.13.0. Contract: https://github.com/tommy-muckstack/myman/blob/main/docs/people-resolve.md.

## Linux and Omarchy

- Calendar proposal candidate (root/Linux 0.15.0, Brain 0.14.0): `myman calendar propose --title TEXT --after ISO --before ISO --time-zone IANA --duration-minutes 30 --json`, action `calendar.propose`, MCP `myman_app_calendar_propose`. Requires human-enabled `calendar_read` AND new default-off `calendar_propose`, both named scopes, and existing OS Calendar access on Mac; Linux/Omarchy uses owner-configured ICS or returns `unsupported_on_platform`. Returns own-calendar candidate slots and an unconfirmed event preview; never books, writes calendar/Brain data, invites, accesses Contacts or checks teammates. Defaults: 15-minute starts, 09:00–18:00 local every day, 30 elapsed minutes, 5 results. Optional `proposed_starts` checks exact offset timestamps instead; `guests` are display labels only. Past/conflicting/out-of-range slots are omitted; no slots means null preview start/end and `complete:false`. See https://github.com/tommy-muckstack/myman/blob/main/docs/calendar-propose.md.
- Calendar free/busy candidate (root/Linux 0.14.0, Brain companion 0.13.0): `myman calendar free --after ISO --before ISO --json` / action `calendar.freebusy` / MCP `myman_app_calendar_freebusy`. Required timestamps include seconds and UTC offsets; maximum 31 elapsed days. Returns only merged busy intervals from the owner's local calendars; teammates remain unknown. Requires the new human-enabled, default-off `calendar_read` grant plus any named credential's scope. Mac also requires existing human-granted OS Calendar access (no automatic prompt); Linux/Omarchy reads owner-configured `calendar.json` + private local ICS or returns `unsupported_on_platform`. No accounts, booking, invitations or Contacts access. `doctor` and `actions calendar.freebusy` report setup; agents cannot enable grants. See https://github.com/tommy-muckstack/myman/blob/main/docs/calendar-freebusy.md for the JSON contract, owner configuration and limits.

- What it is: a Node.js 22+ companion (version 0.13.0 in My Man 1.1.102) for Ubuntu/X11 and Omarchy/Hyprland (Sway also works): screenshots, markup, OCR, video-only screen recording, polished demos, meetings, Voxtype dictation, notes, tasks, Brain search, and the same `myman-app` MCP actions where supported. `myman actions` reports what is supported on Linux.
- Install from a release: download `myman-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `myman-linux-x64.tar.gz.sha256` from https://github.com/tommy-muckstack/myman/releases/latest, then run `sha256sum -c myman-linux-x64.tar.gz.sha256`, `tar -xzf myman-linux-x64.tar.gz`, and `bash myman-linux-x64/scripts/install-linux.sh`. The installer never runs sudo; it prints the optional apt or pacman packages (for example ImageMagick, grim on Wayland, tesseract for OCR, ffmpeg or wf-recorder for recording).
- CLI path: the installer puts the launcher at `~/.local/bin/myman` (programs in `~/.local/share/myman`; `MYMAN_INSTALL_PREFIX` changes `~/.local`). Add `~/.local/bin` to `PATH`. MCP servers: `node ~/.local/share/myman/app-server.mjs` (actions) and `node ~/.local/share/myman/server.mjs` (read-only Brain search). The Brain is `~/MyManBrain`.
- Arch/Omarchy package: `packaging/aur/` has a `myman-bin` PKGBUILD (installs to `/usr/lib/myman`, adds `/usr/bin/myman` and `/usr/bin/myman-setup`). It is not published on the AUR yet, so build it from that folder with `makepkg -si`, then run `myman-setup` once as each user. On Omarchy, `myman omarchy install` adds a SUPER+SHIFT+PRINT "show my agents" key and a MyMan menu.
- Owner grants: `~/.config/myman/agents.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/myman/agents.json`), created with every grant off: `{"version": 1, "grants": {"enabled": false, "capture": false, "markup": false, "recording": false, "library": false, "microphone": false, "control": false, "people_read": false, "calendar_read": false, "calendar_propose": false}}`. Only the owner edits this file; there is no CLI or MCP action that turns a grant on. An optional root-owned `/etc/myman/agents.json` caps them. Check with `myman doctor --json`.
- `myman demo` (one-command product demo, X11 only):
  1. Look: `myman demo --look --app gnome-calculator --json` returns a picture of the app window, a numbered copy with a 50-point grid, and each piece of on-screen text with its click point.
  2. Steps: write a steps file with `wait`, `move`, `click`, `type`, `key` and `scroll` steps. Clicks can name the text to click, for example `{"click": "Play", "caption": "Start the song"}` (`"nth": 2` picks the second match). A `caption` is a short line shown while that step plays.
  3. Dry run: `myman demo --script steps.json --dry-run --json` checks the file and prints the plan and estimated length without opening anything (needs only the `recording` grant).
  4. Run: `myman demo --script steps.json --json` opens the app, records only its window, runs the steps, then polishes the video with zoom, cursor, backdrop, music, and title and end cards. Needs the owner's `recording` and `control` grants.
- Wayland (Omarchy/Hyprland, Sway): screenshots and recording work (grim, wf-recorder), but `myman demo` and `demo --look` are not supported yet because they drive the app with xdotool. Record with `myman record start` and polish with `myman record polish` instead.

## Meeting scheduling intent (step 1, candidate)

- CLI: `myman scheduling parse --input "Coffee with Developer Friday at 10am for 30 min" --json`.
- MCP: `myman_app_scheduling_parse`; action: `scheduling.parse`. Optional arguments: `reference` (ISO instant with offset), `time_zone` (IANA), `use_model` (boolean; CLI `--use-model off`).
- Requires the new default-off `scheduling_parse` grant enabled by the owner in Settings → Agents; named agent scopes must also allow it. Agents cannot enable grants. `doctor` reports the grant.
- Returns title, literal people mentions, day, wall time, duration_minutes, missing fields and issues. Unspecified values stay null; no defaults or email resolution. `needs_clarification` is not booking authorization.
- Pure local rules, optional on-device Foundation Models entity extraction on supported macOS 26+; never reads calendars/Contacts or writes events, sends invites or books. Future booking must show a preview and require a human pressing Book.
- Linux/Omarchy CLI and MCP expose the schema but return `unsupported_on_platform` for this action in step 1.
- Details: https://github.com/tommy-muckstack/myman/blob/main/docs/scheduling-intent.md
